$description: The application frame: the one definition of what Studio's shell IS. Every cell here is a HOST another surface mounts into, and each is addressed by id because TypeScript adopts it (`store.ts`'s initShellRefs, `ui/panel-resize.ts`'s handles) — so the ids are a contract rather than styling, which is also why this document carries no style of its own: the frame must be laid out by the first paint, so its rules are the generated `styles/shell-frame.css` (specs/studio-ui-guidelines.md §1.1).

children.$description: The PANE GRID (studio.md §18.1). One cell per pane, each holding that pane's own strip, jump bar, chrome layer and stage — the four surfaces that used to be flat siblings of THIS grid, which is to say application rows that only ever described one pane. There is nothing to see here in markup: panels/pane-grid.ts reconciles the cells against workspace.panes, because how many there are is a fact about the workspace and a single div can only ever be one of them.

The Bottom dock (⌘J). It sits in the PANE's column, under the stage and above the status bar, so opening it never narrows the Navigator or the Inspector (studio.md §12 region ⑪). Its handle resizes on the other axis; panels/bottom-dock.ts stamps dock.bottom on this host while it is open, and nothing while it is closed.
The Inspector dock. Four tabs — Content · Style · Logic · Assistant (studio.md §12 region ⑨) — all inside this one host.
The app's only status channel: announce what lands in it (studio.md §12 region ⑫).
